title: Competitors with the same name
objective: Check, after a fix for BP-001, that two competitors with the same name can be added, told apart and edited separately.
steps: In a test competition, add two competitors with the same name.
Check both appear as separate rows and as separate entries in 'Enter result'.
Save a result for one of them, rename the other, then remove one.
Reload and check that each action affected only the chosen competitor.
expected_result: Two separate competitors exist; results, renames and removals affect only the chosen one, also after a reload.
reason_manual: The fix needs a person to judge how duplicates should be told apart in the UI (for example a number or birth year).

title: Names with apostrophes, ampersands and accents
objective: Agree which characters names may contain and check that real names with them can be entered and are shown as typed.
steps: Agree with the product owner which characters are allowed (apostrophe, ampersand, hyphen, accents, < and >).
Add names such as O'Neil, D'Angelo, Smith & Co, Åsa Öberg and Jean-Luc.
Check the message for each and how the name appears in the table, the picker, the CSV export and after a reload.
expected_result: Allowed names are added and shown exactly as typed everywhere; rejected names get a message that names the reason.
reason_manual: Which characters are acceptable is a product decision that a person has to make first.

title: Visibility of text fields for low-vision users
objective: Check after a fix for BP-003 that every text field's edge is clearly visible in light and dark mode.
steps: Open the app in light mode and look at the Name, Competitor, Result and Competition name fields without focusing them.
Measure the border (or background) contrast against the card.
Repeat in dark mode and with the operating system's increased-contrast setting.
expected_result: Each field's boundary has at least 3:1 contrast and is easy to see in both themes.
reason_manual: Judging how easy the fields are to see needs a person; the ratio alone does not show that.

title: No sideways page scroll on phones
objective: Check on real phones that the page does not move sideways and only the standings table scrolls horizontally.
steps: On a phone 320-414 px wide (iOS Safari and Android Chrome), open the app.
Swipe the page sideways outside the table.
Swipe inside the standings table.
expected_result: The page itself does not move sideways; only the table scrolls inside its box.
reason_manual: Touch behaviour and real mobile browsers were not part of this audit (Chromium only).

title: Screen reader pass of the main flows
objective: Check what a screen reader user hears when adding a competitor, entering a result and reading the standings.
steps: With VoiceOver (macOS/iOS) or NVDA (Windows), add a competitor and listen to the confirmation.
Choose a competitor and an event with the comboboxes and save a result; then trigger an error.
Move through the standings table and the Edit buttons.
expected_result: Every control is announced with its name and role, success and error messages are announced, and the table is understandable (headers and positions read out).
reason_manual: Needs assistive technology and a person listening; it cannot be judged from the DOM alone.

title: A list holding both disciplines
objective: Check standings, tabs and tab counts when one list holds both decathletes and heptathletes.
steps: In an environment where it is allowed to change General (or another list that holds both disciplines), add two decathletes and two heptathletes with results.
Switch between the Decathlon and Heptathlon tabs.
Compare each tab's count and order with its rows.
expected_result: Each tab shows only its own discipline, sorted by total, and the counts match the rows.
reason_manual: Named competitions hold one discipline; only General holds both, and changing General was out of scope.

title: Scoring across the points tables
objective: Check more values per event against the official World Athletics tables than the audit's sample.
steps: For each event, pick a low, a typical and a near-record value.
Look up the official points for each.
Enter them for a test competitor and compare the points and the total.
expected_result: Every value scores the official points (rounded down) and the total is their sum.
reason_manual: Comparing with the published tables is a desk check by a person who knows the scoring rules.

title: Behaviour when the server is unavailable
objective: Check what the user sees when the server stops responding during normal use.
steps: In a local environment, open the app and then stop the server.
Try to add a competitor, save a result and switch competition.
Start the server again and reload.
expected_result: Each failed action shows a clear message, nothing is shown as saved that was not saved, and the app works again after the server is back.
reason_manual: Stopping the server is outside what the audit was allowed to do.

title: Design review against the intended design
objective: Have a designer compare the pages at 375, 768 and 1280 px in both themes with the intended design.
steps: Open the screenshots in the evidence folder (tpi035-037) or the live app.
Compare spacing, typography, colours and alignment with the design.
expected_result: The pages match the design, or the differences are listed.
reason_manual: There is no design reference; only a designer can judge the result.

title: Main flows in other browsers
objective: Run a short smoke test of the main flows in Firefox and Safari.
steps: In Firefox and Safari, add a competitor, enter a result with a decimal comma and a m:ss time, and check the standings.
Export CSV and save state.
expected_result: The flows behave as in Chromium, with no console errors.

title: Confirmation before Load state replaces data
objective: Decide whether loading a saved file should ask before it replaces a competition's data, and check the chosen behaviour.
steps: Agree with the product owner whether Load state must ask for confirmation.
In a test competition with data, choose 'Load state…' and a saved file.
Check whether the app asks first and that cancelling keeps the data.
expected_result: The app behaves as agreed; if a confirmation is required, cancelling leaves the data unchanged.
reason_manual: Whether a confirmation is required is a product decision; in the audit the file replaced the data at once (EX-032).
